about.title: About this platform
about.intro: This is not a static portfolio — it is a step-by-step research lab with two parallel product tracks. Every feature ships the same way: design the service, expose a typed API, cover it with pytest, wire a browser UI, deploy to Render. The live apps above are phase one; the roadmap below is phases two and three, built in public.
about.method: Each step is a complete vertical slice — backend logic, HTTP contract, tests, and frontend — so progress is visible and auditable, not buried in a todo list.
about.closing: The north star: med-tech-grade tooling — reading systems and sequence analysis that researchers can trust, built with the same rigor I apply to regulated fintech.

tracks.title: Book Notes
tracks.vision: Turn technical reading into a connected knowledge base — searchable, tagged, and AI-assisted across your whole library.
liveToday: Structured notes per book and chapter

tracks.title: Bioinformatics Lab
tracks.vision: A growing suite of sequence tools — from basic composition to cut sites, melting temperature, and translation — each backed by tested API endpoints.
liveToday: DNA: GC content, nucleotide counts, reverse complement
RNA: reverse complement with A↔U pairing
Shared lab UI with live status

topic-thread.promise: Surface related ideas across your entire library — not just within one book.
topic-thread.blurb: LLM-powered connections between notes in different books: shared concepts, contrasting views, follow-up threads. Builds on the existing related-notes agent with library-wide scope and a visual map.
topic-thread.goal: Library-wide semantic links with explainable reasons per connection.

prompt-lens.promise: Describe what you read in plain language; preview structured fields before you save.
prompt-lens.blurb: Extend the extract-from-prompt endpoint into a full preview flow: book, chapter, and note text suggested from a single sentence — you edit, then commit.
prompt-lens.goal: Frictionless capture for readers who think in prose, not forms.

library-radar.promise: One search box across every book, chapter, and note — instant recall.
library-radar.blurb: Cross-book SQLite search with ranked results, snippet context, and jump-to-note navigation. Extends today's per-book search to the full library.
library-radar.goal: Sub-second full-library search with highlighted matches.

tag-shelf.promise: Organize reading by theme — security, biology, systems — not just by book title.
tag-shelf.blurb: Add tags to notes, filter the library by topic, and browse thematic shelves. Pairs with the topic graph for manual curation plus AI discovery.
tag-shelf.goal: Flexible tagging model with filter UI and tagged export.

restriction.promise: Scan DNA against a large enzyme catalog with clear match positions.
restriction.tagline: From sequence to actionable cut map.
restriction.blurb: Loads a broad enzyme list from an online source, lets users select enzymes, and returns precise match positions in one clean workflow.
restriction.goal: Reliable restriction-site scanning with friendly filtering and readable output.

tm.promise: Melting temperature for oligos and short fragments — primer design you can defend.
tm.tagline: Know the heat before the PCR run.
tm.blurb: Nearest-neighbor thermodynamics for short sequences, salt-adjusted defaults, and clear reporting of assumptions. Built for primer sanity checks, not lab replacement.
tm.goal: Reliable Tm for sequences under 100 nt with documented method.

rna-fasta.promise: Drop a .fa file, skip the paste step, run analysis on the whole record.
rna-fasta.blurb: File upload path for RNA Lab mirroring DNA FASTA support — parse headers, validate alphabet, pipe into reverse complement and future RNA endpoints.
rna-fasta.goal: Parity with DNA file input on the RNA side.

translate.promise: Six-frame translation with codon table, start/stop highlights, and readable ORF output.
translate.blurb: Standard genetic code, all six reading frames, longest ORF highlighting, and export-friendly protein sequence. Bridges DNA Lab to protein-level questions.
translate.goal: Correct translation for bacterial/human code table with frame labels.

align.promise: Line up two short sequences — matches, mismatches, gaps — with scores you can explain.
align.blurb: Needleman–Wunsch or Smith–Waterman for educational-scale alignments: visual alignment string, score breakdown, tunable gap penalties.
align.goal: Correct pairwise alignment for sequences up to 500 nt.
